basis: User-reviewed preferences derived only from explicitly authorized SelfGrow, RAG, and VQA project records and selected Codex tasks. Course Q&A, private tasks, all unlisted projects and tasks, credentials, private Vault content, identity claims, and inferred personal experience were excluded.
purpose: Provide an advisory relevance score for newly captured Raw material. The score must never auto-select, reject, delete, or distill content.
preferences: Practical AI, agent, RAG, research, and engineering material that solves real problems and can be reused in projects or working workflows
Clear mechanisms, reproducible steps, source or code evidence, strong baseline comparisons, explicit limitations, and verifiable outcomes
Local-first and privacy-preserving tools with user-owned data, explicit authorization, rollback boundaries, and safe deletion
Simple, native, low-friction implementations with mobile-first interaction and minimal redundant controls, decoration, or dependencies
Clearly scoped workflows that preserve original material and unrelated content, with reviewable proposals before important writes
Minimum viable end-to-end delivery before feature expansion, without sacrificing safety, recoverability, or data integrity
Honest failure states, capability boundaries, and residual risks, with automated verification clearly separated from desktop or mobile real-device acceptance
Evaluation against the strongest relevant baseline and the actual objective, rather than completion rate, architectural complexity, agent count, or proxy metrics
Cost-, latency-, and reliability-aware model workflows, using independent cross-review for higher-risk work without repetitive control that unnecessarily slows execution
Concise, understandable, actionable explanations, supported by diagrams, comparison tables, examples, or bilingual material when they materially improve clarity
A single explicit selfgrow-wiki entry point for repository initialization, selected-Raw discovery, rule-based distillation, relationship linking, and approved structural or preference updates
downrank: Marketing copy, hype, vague trend commentary, unverified claims, or content without usable mechanisms or evidence
Complex architectures, agent stacking, premature expansion, or speculative features without measured benefit for the current problem
Automatic selection, distillation, deletion, hidden writes, or broad mutations that bypass user review and approval
Shallow lists, repeated summaries, author promotion, untraceable output, or material that adds no durable knowledge
Solutions that optimize proxy metrics, underperform the strongest relevant baseline while claiming success, or hide failures, costs, and applicability limits

rubric.0-39: Weak fit or low-signal material with little reusable value
rubric.40-59: Some relevance but limited evidence, novelty, or practical depth
rubric.60-79: Useful and aligned material worth reviewing
rubric.80-100: Strongly aligned, evidence-rich, reusable material with clear practical value
